title: The content layers
html:
English | Português (Brasil)

The content layers

The first question from anyone adopting the kit is "where does what my AI carries come from?" — and the answer is a scale of four layers, weakest to strongest: L0 embedded (the minimal BASE inside the binary — offline), L1 FULL (the 93 workflow components, embedded), L2 packs (the organization overlays and the knowledge state packs) and L3 local (the operator's creations). When two layers provide the same component, the precedence is: local > pack > full > base — your fine-tuning wins, the embedded loses.

The two profiles — and the operator's choice

When the operator ran golmet install --engine opencode (tutorial 00), the wizard asked for the profile. essencial installs L0+BASE into the workspace .golmet/ zone — the kit becomes versioned in the repository and the team inherits by cloning; it works on any agentic engine. completo materializes L1 FULL into the engine — the 93 components (agents, skills, profiles, templates) live in Opencode, and it is the recommended mode because nothing is missing: the AI enters the workspace with the whole workflow.

Local customization of a managed file is detected and preserved — the content manifest knows every file's provenance and SHA-256; overwriting what the operator modified requires an explicit --force.

The .golmet/ zone changes role

The same kit folder, different semantics by context — and that is by design: in the product workspace, .golmet/ is the repo-versioned kit (DR-008); in the engine config, it's kit state (the content manifest and the personal.json); in an org-repo Organization, it's the gitignored work zone (checkpoints in meetings/, history in migrations/) — with the versioned exception .golmet/skills/ when the org essential runs at the root (see organization.md).

What it means in MeuApp's practice: the product carries no zone of its own — the zone is MinhaOrganizacao'. If the org ever moved to produtos-repo, each product would gain its own (init --into delivers the declared model — the detail in docs/reference/commands.md).
